text_blocks.snippet: The most common scams reported across Central Illinois include fake text messages from state agencies, aggressive law enforcement impersonation calls, and seasonal home improvement schemes.
You can report any suspected fraudulent activity directly to the Federal Trade Commission Reporting Portal .

list.snippet: 📱 State Agency and Toll Text Scams
Scammers send text messages pretending to be the Illinois Secretary of State or tollway services.
Messages claim you owe money for traffic violations or vehicle registration.
Threaten license suspension to panic you into clicking a malicious link.
Callers claim to be from local sheriff's offices (such as Macon County) .
Claim you missed jury duty or have an active warrant.
Demand immediate payment or personal information to clear the citation.
Unlicensed contractors target neighborhoods offering cheap driveway sealing or roofing repairs .
Take large cash down payments and never return to complete the work.
Fake rental listings use stolen photos from local real estate sites at prices that are "too good to be true" .
High-dollar social media marketplace scams are rising across regional counties like Peoria.
Never click links in unsolicited text messages claiming to be from state or DMV offices. State agencies do not text for fee payments.
Hang up immediately if a caller claims to be law enforcement demanding money or gift card/crypto payments.
Verify independently by looking up the official phone number of the agency or business and calling them back directly.
Check contractors thoroughly, refuse high upfront cash payments, and verify local licensing before hiring.
